items.title: Direct summands of relatively finitely presented modules are relatively finitely presented
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For f : X -> S locally of finite type, if F direct-sum F' is finitely presented relative to S then each summand is (the author's retained slogan: A direct summand of a module inherits the property of being finitely presented relative to a base) — the retract-closure law of the relative-presentation cone, used to pass from ambient trivial bundles to subbundles in the chapter's flattening stratification arguments. The retained proof is written: translation into schemes of the algebra theorem More on Algebra, lemma sum-relatively-finite-presentation; through the sibling dictionary (card L16180) the assertion becomes the ring-level statement that relative finite presentation is stable under direct summands, whose proof (idempotent splitting of a finite presentation) lives in the cited algebra lemma. Retained author proof at lines 16569-16574.
